title: OOP Debugging Challenge
summary: Hunt down tricky runtime polymorphic bugs, NullPointerExceptions, and state mutation errors.

activities.title: Practical Context: Production Incident Troubleshooting

realWorldMetaphor.scenario: When an aircraft deviates unexpectedly from its glide slope during an automated landing, the crash investigation team doesn't make random guesses. They pull the digital flight data recorder ('black box'), syncing the pilot input commands (reference types) with the actual wing hydraulic control surfaces (runtime heap objects) second by second until they locate the exact sensor inversion that caused the anomaly.
realWorldMetaphor.mapping: In complex OOP applications, bugs rarely manifest as simple syntax errors. They appear as ClassCastExceptions in polymorphic queues, field hiding anomalies returning default 0s, or mutable reference leaks mutating customer balances behind the scenes. Systematic debugging requires inspecting object references on the stack against heap instances and vtables.
realWorldMetaphor.takeaway: Effective OOP debugging requires separating compile-time reference expectations from runtime heap realities.

activities.content:
When software bugs escape into staging or production, engineers must diagnose the root cause under pressure.

OOP bugs often manifest as subtle runtime exceptions (`ClassCastException`, `NullPointerException`, or state corruption) resulting from misaligned references or broken contracts.

This hands-on challenge equips you with a systematic protocol to inspect and resolve complex object-oriented failures.

activities.title: OOP Debugging Challenge: Root Cause Analysis and Troubleshooting Protocol
Anatomy of the Constructor Override Initialization Trap
activities.explanation: Illustrates why calling overridable methods inside constructors is catastrophic in Java: the superclass constructor invokes the subclass override before subclass fields are initialized, causing NPE.

stepByStepWalkthrough.description: `new SmartSensor()` begins by executing `BaseDevice()` superclass constructor.
Because of dynamic dispatch, `SmartSensor.initHardware()` is called.
At this point in time, `sensorId` has NOT yet been initialized (it is `null`). `sensorId.toLowerCase()` throws NullPointerException!

activities.title: The Refactored Robust Fix
activities.explanation: Separating construction from initialization ensures that all instance fields are assigned before any polymorphic overrides run.

stepByStepWalkthrough.description: `SafeBaseDevice` constructor avoids calling any overridable methods.
`sensor.initialize()` runs polymorphically with fully initialized state.

questions.question: Why is calling an overridable method from a constructor considered a dangerous anti-pattern?
options: It causes a stack overflow error immediately
The subclass override will execute before the subclass constructor has initialized its own fields, reading null/default values
It prevents the JVM from creating heap objects
It turns all fields into static variables
questions.explanation: In Java, superclass constructors execute before subclass field initializers. Invoking an override during super() runs against uninitialized fields.

questions.question: What is the result if a subclass constructor throws an exception?
options: The object is partially constructed and remains accessible via garbage collector roots
The constructor fails, the object reference is not returned, and the half-constructed object is eligible for garbage collection
All superclasses remain active in memory forever
questions.explanation: If a constructor throws an exception, no reference is returned to the caller; the abandoned object will be collected by the GC.

questions.question: When debugging a ClassCastException, what tool is most effective to inspect the actual runtime type?
questions.explanation: Calling `getClass().getName()` prints the true underlying concrete class instantiated in heap memory.

questions.question: How can you detect if an object has leaked a mutable internal list?
options: Check if the class implements Serializable
Mutate the list returned by the getter and check if the object's internal representation changed
questions.explanation: If modifying the returned collection alters the object's internal state, a reference leak exists.

questions.question: What happens if a class declares `public int count = 10;` and its subclass declares `public int count = 20;`, and you write `Base b = new Sub(); System.out.println(b.count);`?
options: Prints 10 (field hiding resolves by reference type)
questions.explanation: Field resolution is static and determined by the declared reference type (`Base`), which holds 10.

questions.question: What tool in modern IDEs helps identify field hiding and mutable reference leaks automatically?
options: Static analysis linters (SonarQube, ErrorProne, SpotBugs, IntelliJ Inspections)
questions.explanation: Static analysis linters flag field hiding and leaked mutable references during build time.

questions.question: If an object is placed in a HashSet and then one of its fields used in hashCode() is modified, what occurs?
options: The HashSet updates the bucket automatically
The object remains in the old bucket and set.contains(obj) returns false
questions.explanation: The hash table looks for the object in the new hash bucket and fails to find it, turning it into a ghost.

questions.question: What is the best way to prevent calling overridable methods in constructors?
options: Make the helper methods private or final
questions.explanation: `private` or `final` methods cannot be overridden by subclasses, making them safe to call from constructors.

questions.question: What is the symptom of an accidental method overload instead of override?
options: The compiler refuses to build the code
Dynamic dispatch fails to invoke the subclass method when called through a superclass reference
questions.explanation: If parameter types differ slightly, the subclass merely overloaded the method; calls through the superclass invoke the parent method.

questions.question: How does `@Override` prevent accidental method overloading bugs?
options: It converts the method into a final method
It forces the compiler to verify that the method actually matches a superclass method signature, causing a compile error if it does not
It bypasses the virtual method table
questions.explanation: The `@Override` annotation turns a silent overloading bug into an immediate compile-time error.

interviewQA.question: Describe a scenario where calling an overridable method in a constructor caused a production incident.
interviewQA.answer: A base class `AbstractCacheService` called `initCache()` in its constructor. A concrete subclass `RedisCacheService` had an inline field `private JedisPool pool = new JedisPool();`. When `new RedisCacheService()` was called, the base constructor invoked `initCache()`, which attempted to connect using `pool`. Because subclass field initializers hadn't executed yet, `pool` was `null`, throwing an unexpected `NullPointerException` during application startup.
interviewQA.expectedAnswer: Superclass constructor calls overridable method before subclass fields are initialized, causing NullPointerException on uninitialized fields.
interviewQA.keyTakeaway: Never call overridable methods from constructors.
keyPoints: Never call overridable methods from constructors.

interviewQA.question: How do you debug an intermittent `NullPointerException` occurring in an asynchronous event pipeline?
interviewQA.answer: 1) Check for race conditions where shared mutable objects are being modified concurrently without volatile or synchronization barriers. 2) Inspect constructor reference publication to verify that the `this` reference did not escape before the constructor completed. 3) Replace shared mutable state with immutable event DTOs (e.g. Java records) to guarantee thread safety.
interviewQA.expectedAnswer: Check for concurrent race conditions, constructor reference escaping, and replace mutable state with immutable records.
interviewQA.keyTakeaway: Replace shared mutable pipeline state with immutable records to eliminate asynchronous NPEs.
keyPoints: Replace shared mutable pipeline state with immutable records to eliminate asynchronous NPEs.

interviewQA.question: What is 'this escaping' during construction, and why is it dangerous?
interviewQA.answer: 'This escaping' occurs when a constructor passes `this` to another thread or registers `this` as an event listener before the constructor finishes executing. The receiving thread can then observe the object in a partially initialized, inconsistent state, leading to subtle race conditions and corrupted data.
interviewQA.expectedAnswer: 'This escaping' exposes a partially constructed object to other threads, violating initialization safety.

interviewQA.question: How do you detect and fix accidental method overloading bugs in large legacy codebases?
interviewQA.answer: 1) Enforce the compiler flag `-Xlint:overrides` to warn on missing `@Override` annotations. 2) Use static analysis tools (e.g. ErrorProne or SpotBugs) to catch mismatched parameter types. 3) Systematically annotate all intended overrides with `@Override`, turning subtle signature drift into explicit compiler errors.
interviewQA.expectedAnswer: Enforce @Override annotations and static analysis tools like ErrorProne to catch signature mismatches.
interviewQA.keyTakeaway: Always use @Override to catch accidental overloading at compile time.
keyPoints: Always use @Override to catch accidental overloading at compile time.

interviewQA.question: What steps do you take when a `ClassCastException` is reported in production logs?
interviewQA.answer: 1) Identify the exact line of code and the source and target types from the stack trace. 2) Trace where the object was instantiated and entered the pipeline. 3) Determine why an unexpected subtype arrived (e.g. a deserialization error or unvalidated generic collection cast). 4) Replace the unsafe cast with pattern matching `if (obj instanceof ExpectedType t)` or refactor the pipeline to use strongly-typed generics.
interviewQA.expectedAnswer: Analyze stack trace for source/target types, locate where object originated, and replace blind cast with pattern matching or generics.
interviewQA.keyTakeaway: Replace blind downcasts with pattern matching and strong typing.
keyPoints: Replace blind downcasts with pattern matching and strong typing.

interviewQA.question: Why is defensive copying necessary even if a class is internal to an engineering team?
interviewQA.answer: Because software systems evolve. Even within a team, another engineer might reuse a list or modify an array after passing it to an entity, inadvertently creating action-at-a-distance bugs. Defensive copying establishes a rigid boundary that prevents subtle bugs regardless of how the calling code changes in the future.
interviewQA.expectedAnswer: Defensive copying guarantees robust encapsulation and protects against accidental future developer modifications.
interviewQA.keyTakeaway: Defensive copying protects systems from future changes and maintenance regressions.
keyPoints: Defensive copying protects systems from future changes and maintenance regressions.

practiceProblems.title: Warmup: Debugging Overridden Constructor Bug
practiceProblems.problemStatement: The code below fails with a `NullPointerException` because the base class constructor calls the overridable method `setup()`, which attempts to format `configCode` before the subclass has initialized it. Fix the bug by making `setup()` private in `BaseService` or by calling it explicitly after construction, ensuring the program prints `'Configured: PROD-101'`.
hints: Remove setup() from the BaseService constructor.
Call ms.setup() in main after the object is completely constructed.

practiceProblems.title: Debug Hidden Field Configuration Leak
practiceProblems.problemStatement:
Fix the configuration loader from scratch without starter code:
1. Base class `DbConfig` with `protected int maxPoolSize = 10`.
2. Subclass `HighThroughputConfig extends DbConfig` that accidentally redeclared `protected int maxPoolSize = 50`, causing `DbConfig.getMaxPoolSize()` to return 10 instead of 50.
3. Implement proper encapsulation: make `maxPoolSize` private in `DbConfig`, take it in the constructor `DbConfig(int size)`, provide getter `getMaxPoolSize()`, and have `HighThroughputConfig` pass 50 to `super(50)`.
4. In `Main`, create `DbConfig cfg = new HighThroughputConfig();`.
5. Print `'Max Pool: ' + cfg.getMaxPoolSize()` (should print `'Max Pool: 50'`).
hints: Avoid declaring maxPoolSize in the subclass.

practiceProblems.title: Debug Leaked Mutable Collection in Immutable Class
practiceProblems.problemStatement:
Design and debug an immutable `SecurityToken` from scratch without starter code:
1. Class `SecurityToken` marked final.
2. Fields: `private final String tokenId` and `private final List<String> permissions`.
3. Constructor `SecurityToken(String tokenId, List<String> permissions)`: must perform a defensive copy using `List.copyOf` or `new ArrayList<>(permissions)`.
4. Getter `getPermissions()`: must return `Collections.unmodifiableList(permissions)`.
5. In `Main`:
   - Create a mutable list `perms = ["READ", "WRITE"]`
   - Instantiate `SecurityToken token = new SecurityToken("tok-100", perms);`
   - Mutate original list: `perms.add("ADMIN_DELETE")`
   - Print `'Token permissions count: ' + token.getPermissions().size()` (must be 2)
   - Verify modifying returned list throws an exception, catching it and printing `'Immutable protection verified'`.
practiceProblems.expectedOutput:
Token permissions count: 2
Immutable protection verified
hints: Defensive copy in constructor protects from `perms.add("ADMIN_DELETE")`.
Unmodifiable list in getter throws UnsupportedOperationException when `.add("HACK")` is called.

practiceProblems.title: Bug Hunt: Accidental Overloading Mismatch
practiceProblems.problemStatement: A developer intended to override `equals(Object o)` in `Product`, but accidentally declared `public boolean equals(Product p)`. Because of this signature mismatch, `HashSet` and polymorphic collections invoke `Object.equals(Object)`, treating two products with identical IDs as different objects! Fix the code by properly annotating `@Override` and matching the exact `Object` signature so that `p1.equals(p2)` returns `true` and the output is `'Equal products: true'`.
hints: Change parameter type from `Product p` to `Object obj`.
Use pattern matching `if (obj instanceof Product p)`.

practiceProblems.title: Advanced: Diagnostic Black Box Telemetry Pipeline
practiceProblems.problemStatement:
Build a multi-fault diagnostic telemetry parser from scratch without starter code:
1. Interface `TelemetryPacket` with `long getTimestamp()` and `String getPacketType()`.
2. Class `GpsPacket implements TelemetryPacket`: fields `timestamp` (long), `latitude` (double), `longitude` (double). Implements interface methods (`getPacketType()` returns `"GPS"`). Methods `getLatitude()`, `getLongitude()`.
3. Class `EnginePacket implements TelemetryPacket`: fields `timestamp` (long), `rpm` (int), `temp` (double). Implements interface methods (`getPacketType()` returns `"ENGINE"`). Methods `getRpm()`, `getTemp()`.
4. Class `TelemetryAuditor` with static method `public static void audit(TelemetryPacket[] packets)`:
   - Loops over packets safely (skips null packets)
   - Uses pattern matching for `instanceof`:
     - If `GpsPacket g`: prints `'[GPS @ ' + g.getTimestamp() + '] Lat: ' + g.getLatitude() + ', Lon: ' + g.getLongitude()`
     - If `EnginePacket e`: prints `'[ENGINE @ ' + e.getTimestamp() + '] RPM: ' + e.getRpm() + ', Temp: ' + e.getTemp() + 'C'`
5. In `Main`, test with an array containing:
   - `new GpsPacket(1000L, 37.7749, -122.4194)`
   - `new EnginePacket(1050L, 3200, 88.5)`
   - `null`
Verify that all packets are parsed safely without ClassCastException or NullPointerException.
hints: Pattern matching automatically handles `null` packets by evaluating to false.
Safe downcasting prints GPS coordinates and Engine telemetry accurately.
